specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** dublin-core-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of ten pieces of information about a resource under the Dublin Core element that holds it, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** The Metadata Metric, Metadata Record, Dublin Core (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each piece of information the learner commits one of eleven elements. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct element column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the element table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The author's name belongs in Contributor. (2) The license belongs in Description. (3) The format of a file is its type. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying information by field is an Understand-level action that a reviewer performs when reading or writing a record. Ten distinct fields teach the learner what each element is for. **Content:** The eleven elements offered: Title, Creator, Subject, Description, Date, Type, Format, Identifier, Source, Language, Rights. The ten pieces of information: | # | Information shown to the learner | Correct element | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Maria Lopez | Creator | The person mainly responsible for the resource. | | 2 | https://example.org/watershed-basics | Identifier | An unambiguous reference to the resource. | | 3 | en | Language | The language of the content. | | 4 | 2025-03-14 | Date | A date in the resource's life. | | 5 | CC BY 4.0 with a link to the license | Rights | The license is the rights statement. | | 6 | A short reading and quiz that explain what a watershed is. | Description | A summary of the content. | | 7 | Watersheds; Water cycle | Subject | The topics of the resource. | | 8 | InteractiveResource | Type | The kind of resource. | | 9 | text/html | Format | The file format or medium. | | 10 | Adapted from an earlier lesson plan | Source | A resource from which this one is derived. | **Provenance:** The pieces of information are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The element definitions follow the chapter section "Dublin Core". **Rules:** Each piece of information has exactly one correct element, and the ten correct elements are all different. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one piece of information and the eleven elements. 2. The learner may open the element table. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses an element, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After item 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 items in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [element]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This belongs in [element]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can file information in a record." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed item. **Starting State:** The first item, the eleven elements, and the element table closed. The question shown is "Which Dublin Core element holds this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says Dublin Core has 15 core elements, that the rubric's author field is Creator and its license field is Rights, and that grade level uses the education level term.
